explanation: The downstream result is faulty because all priority rows have upstream_rank 0 even though the evidence_sources handoff contains ranks 1 through 8. The mismatch is introduced upstream: assemble_provenance writes each provenance row with record_id equal to source_id, producing evidence record identities like s01, while downstream needs and coverage rows use record identities n06-r01 through n06-r08. That breaks the stipulated record identity/provenance handoff and prevents downstream prioritization from preserving upstream provenance order.
cited_evidence: Job-2 input evidence_sources contains record_id values s01 through s08 with ranks 1 through 8, while Job-2 input needs contains record_id values n06-r01 through n06-r08.
Observed Job-2 priorities show upstream_rank: 0 for every record, including n06-r01 through n06-r08, so provenance rank order was not preserved.
Upstream assemble_provenance source appends {'record_id': record.get('source_id', ''), 'source_id': record.get('source_id', ''), ...}, replacing the need record_id with the source_id.

Downstream prioritize builds rank_by_record_id from evidence_sources record_id and looks up coverage record_id, so evidence record_id values s01..s08 cannot match coverage record_id values n06-r01..n06-r08.
